reports.description: Generate the one shared toy season (3 creators, 5 manufacturers, molds, releases, shelves, bags, videos, retention curves, links and clicks) from a seed. The structure is fixed; the seed varies only the numbers.

guarantees.description: Every terminal has its declared type and every reference resolves to an instance of the right frame.
No hard expectation (one without a mismatch rule) is violated by the generated world.
Creator names, channel titles, manufacturer names, mold names, video titles and bag names are unique, so a name on the page points at one thing.
Generating twice from the same seed gives the same bytes.

reports.description: Cross-link the whole world: card/mark→appearance→disc→mold→manufacturer→release, click→link→video→card, video→bag→sponsor deal. Mismatches are resolved by the frames' own alternate frames and transformations.

guarantees.description: Every violated soft expectation was handled by the alternate frame or transformation its mismatch names, and every handler fired because of a violation.
No hard expectation (mismatch = null) is violated anywhere in the world: bad data is rejected, never explained away.
Every terminal value has its declared type and every reference resolves to an instance of the right frame.
Every alternate frame instance meets its own (inherited and added) hard expectations: inheriting did not break the invariants.
Every edge joins two things that exist (instances, appearances or alternate-frame instances).
Every appearance links to a disc, a video, and (if it has a card) a card; every disc links to a mold or a provisional mold.
The sponsor bucket the OtherBrandAppearance frame carried equals a direct lookup of the deals active on the video's local publish day.
Every click is credited to one moment, to the disc in the video, or explicitly to nothing (with a reason), never two at once.
Every appearance lies inside its video and has positive length.

reports.description: Attention-seconds per appearance, disc-in-video, disc and mold (Shorts and long videos reported apart), through thro.attentionSeconds and statistics.sum.

guarantees.description: Attention is between 0 and views x seconds on screen x the largest retention fraction (a looping Short can pass 1).
Attention is null exactly when retention is unavailable (no views / no Studio / no curve), and never a silent zero.
Every computed attention value carries a Capability Lab receipt rooted at thro.attentionSeconds.
Disc totals equal the sum of their disc-in-video totals, and Short + long equals the total.

reports.description: Retention inside each card vs the seconds around it, through thro.retentionDip (statistics.mean).

guarantees.description: dipped is true exactly when the drop exceeds 0.05.

reports.description: Which videos sit around a release date, and at what offset (a range when the date is only a month), using each release's own window length.

guarantees.description: pre-release ⇔ offsets negative; release-window ⇔ 0..windowDays; established ⇔ over windowDays.

reports.description: Clicks per link/disc, how each is credited, days after publish, and clicks per 1,000 attention-seconds (thro.ratio).

guarantees.description: Per-link counts add up to the number of clicks; moment + video + unattributed = total.

reports.description: Viewer-minutes on screen per sponsor (or other brand) per quarter across creators (overlapping cards counted once), through thro.attentionSeconds and thro.ratio.

guarantees.description: Counting overlapping cards once never gives more than adding the cards' attention separately.
Each entry's viewer-minutes equal its union attention-seconds / 60.
A row with nothing measurable has viewer-minutes null (never 0); a measurable row has a number; a partial row says so.
Short and long viewer-minutes add up to the row total.

reports.description: Verify one Case against the shared season: valid world, all Calculations pass, the pipeline equals an independent recomputation from raw JSON, the departure has an observable and local effect, the failed expectation selected what its mismatch string names, and the claim of the Case holds.

guarantees.description: All checks of the Case pass.
A Case states what it expects: an expectation of the world, a change in linked results, or sentences.

reports.description: How cross-linked the dataset is: one connected world, every reference resolving, entities shared by several Cases, no island Cases, rollups across creators per sponsor and per mold, unique names.

guarantees.description: The world is a single connected component (every instance reaches every other through references).
No reference points at something that does not exist.
At least 120 entities (discs, videos, molds, releases, deals, bags, links, clicks, cards, curves) appear in two or more Cases.
Every Case shares at least one such entity with another Case.
The Cases, linked through shared entities, form one connected network.
At least 2 sponsor-view rows add up more than one creator, and every brand that has discs with several creators has such a row.
At least 5 molds appear with more than one creator and have one combined total.
A mold's combined attention equals the sum of its creators' parts.
Every disc has its own label (brand, mold, plastic, run, owner) so no two discs read the same.
Counting every instance except the Click leaves (each click is one edge by nature), the average number of references in and out is at least 4.

The Cases include the boundary situations the product cares about (deal first / last day, release day, window edges, click at a card's last second, quarter edge, month precision, time zone, chained frames).
Every terminal of every input frame either changes some result or sentence in at least one Case, or is listed with the reason it cannot.

the curve must cover the video (hard expectation coversVideo): shorter is an invalid world and longer changes nothing a reader sees
